name: Morph
oneLiner: Full VMs with memory-and-disk snapshots, branched into parallel copies, billed in MCUs.
whatItIs: Morph Cloud sells devboxes and lower-level instances: full virtual machines that can run Docker-in-Docker, a local Kubernetes cluster or a self-hosted database.
Its distinctive primitive is the snapshot: an immutable copy of memory and disk that can boot a new instance with running processes, or branch into many copies for fan-out.
whoFor: Teams running parallel agent environments, RL rollouts or test fan-out, and developers who want a cloud devbox with a dashboard.
isolation: Full virtual machine, with Docker-in-Docker, systemd and root documented. FUSE is available; nested virtualisation and other guest operating systems are experimental.
sizes: Resources are chosen at creation: vCPU, memory and disk size. No complete size catalogue, GPU statement, region list or data-residency commitment is published.

billing.model: Prepaid MCUs with optional monthly plans that include an allocation.
billing.meter: One MCU covers 1 vCPU-hour, 4 GB RAM-hours, 16 GB disk-hours or 5 TB snapshot-hours. The rate is the maximum of those dimensions, at $0.05 per MCU-hour.
billing.stopped: A paused instance bills only for the snapshot taken. A stopped instance is deleted, so its own disk is not a cheap parked state.
billing.planFee: Developer $0, Team $40 and Scale $250 a month, including 0, 1,000 and 7,500 MCUs.
billing.minimum: No published minimum duration. The signup docs promise 300 free compute hours a month; the pricing page shows 0 MCUs and asks you to buy.

facts.label: Legal entity
facts.value: Morph Labs, Inc., at a San Francisco address. The state of incorporation is not published.

facts.label: Founded
facts.value: 2023, by Jesse Han, per Tracxn. Christian Szegedy is reported as chief scientist and a seed investor.

facts.label: Funding
facts.value: Disputed: one source reports a $5.75M Khosla-led seed, another says no funding has been raised.

source.quote: Morph Labs has not raised any funding yet.

facts.label: Headcount
facts.value: About 9–11, an aggregator estimate for 2026. No company-confirmed figure.

facts.label: Status and SLA
facts.value: Status page reports 100% for the Cloud API over its 90-day chart. No numeric SLA is published.

facts.label: Certification
facts.value: No verified SOC 2 for Morph Labs, Inc. The Delve trust portal sometimes cited for it belongs to AutoInfra.

well: Full VMs with Docker-in-Docker, systemd, root and FUSE, for a workload that needs a normal server.
Snapshots of memory and disk that branch into several running instances.
A configurable machine: vCPU, memory and disk are chosen at creation rather than picked from a menu.
badly: A buyer who needs published regions, GPU options, maximum sizes or an SLA.
An attached block volume: Morph Volumes is S3-compatible object storage behind a gateway.
A compliance review that expects a SOC 2 naming Morph Labs, Inc.

usability.dashboard: A devbox dashboard can create a machine from a template or snapshot and open it in VS Code.
usability.withoutCode: A devbox can be created without API code, but setup asks for an SDK or CLI and an API key.
usability.signup: An invite is mentioned in the signup docs; card requirement and waitlist status are not published.
usability.docs: Documentation covers devboxes, instances, snapshots, volumes and agent tokens. No independent status page was verified.
tripsUp: Stop deletes the instance; pause is the state-preserving action.
Booting a snapshot is a cold boot; starting it restores memory.
Volumes are S3-compatible object storage, not an attached block disk.
The free-credit promise contradicts the pricing page.

caveats.issue: Free credit is described two ways
caveats.detail: Signup docs promise 300 free compute hours a month on the $0 Developer plan; the pricing page lists 0 MCUs and says to purchase MCUs to use compute.

evidence.quote: Once you have your invite, our $0/month Developer Plan provides 300 free compute hours per month

caveats.detail: The stop API releases the instance and its resources; only a separately retained snapshot survives.
Whether snapshots bill allocated or stored bytes, and how compression and deduplication count, is not stated.
Morph Volumes is an S3-compatible product accessed through a gateway and CLI, distinct from an attached disk or EFS mount.

caveats.issue: No published region, GPU or architecture list
caveats.detail: Host locations, data residency and GPU availability were not confirmed in primary material.

strengths: Snapshots capture memory, processes and disk, and are immutable.
Branch one snapshot into many running instances.
Full VMs with Docker-in-Docker and systemd.
A devbox dashboard for creating and opening environments.
